title: Visors on the bandstand and the sleeping drummer again
summary: The band wore visors against a dim light bulb, and Moore marvels once more at the sleeping drummer.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I see. Okay. Let's see, you were at the La Vida Ballroom, okay, with Kid Rene' and how about the decorum of the bandstand, what the musicians dressed in and so forth?
Yes, well, they had an overhead light, only one little dim light bulb and in order to have -- the bulb always hurt your eyes so everyone in the band wore a visor.
So they looked like editors instead of musicians?

Right. Right. That drummer had one of the longest visors -- the front of the visor was sticking way out -- so he could sleep. But he was all right when he'd wake up. The rhythm never stops. That's phenomenal. It's hard to believe. I had to look at him, doing my double-takes many nights.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
I'd look at him. He's down there sound asleep, he's playing. Playing. It's hard to believe it.
